questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) What is automatic speech recognition (ASR)? Describe one situation in which it can be used. (3 marks)

(b) Give two advantages of ASR. (2 marks)

(c) Give one limitation of ASR. (1 mark)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Definition and one use (3 marks)**

**Automatic speech recognition (ASR)** is the technology by which a computer (a microphone, a sound card and recognition software) converts **spoken words into text or into commands**. The sound wave is digitised, broken into small units (phonemes), compared with an acoustic model and a dictionary/language model, and the most probable words are output.

**One situation:** a doctor, lawyer or journalist **dictates** a report or letter directly into a word processor instead of typing it; other uses are voice commands on a smartphone or in a car (hands-free calling, navigation), voice-operated telephone banking or call-centre menus, and help for users with a physical disability.

**(b) Two advantages (2 marks)**

- It is **faster than typing** (speech is about 120 to 150 words per minute against 30 to 40 for most typists).
- It is **hands-free and eyes-free**, so it can be used while driving, operating machinery or during surgery, and it helps people who cannot use a keyboard or mouse (motor impairment, blindness); it also reduces repetitive strain injury.

**(c) One limitation (1 mark)**

It makes **recognition errors** with strong accents, background noise, homophones (to/too/two) or technical words, so the text must be proofread; it also needs a quiet place and, often, a period of training for the user's voice.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Briefly explain the activities of an operating system with regards to the following:

(a) File Management. (2 marks)

(b) Memory Management. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) File management (2 marks)**

The operating system organises data on the backing store (hard disk, flash drive) into **files and folders (directories)** in a hierarchy. It **creates, names, opens, copies, moves, renames and deletes** files, keeps a table recording **where each file is stored** on the disk (for example the file allocation table) and which space is free, and controls **access rights** (who can read, write or execute a file) and file security.

**(b) Memory management (2 marks)**

The operating system **allocates main memory (RAM)** to each program and its data when it is loaded, **keeps track of which locations are in use and which are free**, **protects** the memory of one program from the others, and **releases** the space when a program ends. When RAM is not enough it uses **virtual memory** (swapping or paging parts of programs between RAM and a space on the hard disk).

questions.enonce_markdown:
A company uses video-conference to discuss pertinent issues affecting the company.

(a) What is video conferencing? (1 mark)

(b) State TWO advantages to the company of having a video-conference. (2 marks)

(c) What is the impact of transmission bandwidth on the system? (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Video conferencing (1 mark)**

It is a **real-time communication service** in which two or more people in different places **see and hear each other** at the same time, using cameras, microphones, screens and loudspeakers connected through a network (usually the Internet) and conferencing software.

**(b) Two advantages to the company (2 marks)**

- It **saves travel time and cost** (tickets, accommodation, allowances): managers in different towns or countries meet from their offices.
- Meetings can be held **quickly and at short notice** with many participants, so decisions are taken faster; documents and screens can be shared and the meeting can be recorded (other acceptable points: less lost working time, lower pollution, easier to involve experts).

**(c) Impact of transmission bandwidth (2 marks)**

Bandwidth is the amount of data the link can carry per second. Sound and video need a large data rate. With a **high bandwidth** the pictures are clear and smooth and the sound is synchronised, with few delays. With a **low bandwidth** the picture is blurred, jerky or frozen, the sound breaks up or lags behind the picture, the delay (latency) increases and the connection may drop, especially when many participants share the same link. (Compression and lowering the picture quality are used to reduce the demand.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
To convert a binary number to its 2's complement, do the following:

- Reverse each bit.
- Add 1 to the resulting number.

(a) Calculate the 2's complement of 101110 (1 mark)

(b) Give one use of the 2's compliment in the computer. (1 mark)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) 2's complement of 101110 (1 mark)**

1. Reverse each bit of $101110$: $010001$.
2. Add 1: $010001 + 1 = 010010$.

**The 2's complement of 101110 is 010010** (on 6 bits). Check: $101110_2 = 46$ unsigned, and $46 + 18 = 64 = 2^6$, so $010010_2 = 18$ is the 2's complement of $101110_2$ (that is, 101110 represents $-18$ in 6-bit two's complement notation).

**(b) One use (1 mark)**

The 2's complement is used to **represent negative integers** in binary. It lets the ALU carry out **subtraction as an addition** ($A - B = A + \text{2's complement of } B$), so the processor does not need a separate subtraction circuit.
